tagline: Plan your workouts, log every set and watch your records and progress grow, with optional AI help.
description:
Fitness is a training log for each Apps Hub profile. Build your own workouts, log every set in the desktop app or on its public web page, and see how much you lifted, ran or held, set by set.

Workouts and exercises
Choose from about 95 ready-made exercises with names in all nine interface languages, or add your own. Every exercise is counted the way it should be: weight and reps, reps only, a held time, distance and time, or cardio time. Build a workout from exercises with their sets and targets, link exercises into supersets, or run it as a circuit or as work and rest intervals. Plan your week by choosing the days each workout belongs to.

Training
Start a workout and the app plans every set for you, with what you did last time shown next to it. Mark sets as done, mark warm-up sets and sets to failure, use the rest timer between sets and a stopwatch for timed sets, and add or remove exercises on the way. Finish with the length and date corrected if needed and see the estimated calories.

Records and statistics
For every exercise you get your heaviest weight, estimated one-rep max, best set and workout volume, most reps, longest time and distance and best pace, plus the best weight for each number of reps and a chart of how each exercise grew. A new record is celebrated as it happens. Overview shows workouts, time, calories, weight lifted and distance, a weekly chart, an activity calendar, sets per muscle group and your streak toward your own weekly goal.

Units and health
Weights and distances follow your region, pounds and miles in the United States, kilograms and kilometres elsewhere, while everything is stored in kilograms and kilometres. Calories are an estimate and not a measurement. With Health installed, each profile can choose to send workout minutes and calories to Health, take body data from it, and see activity that other apps sent there.
capabilities: About 95 ready-made exercises with names in all nine interface languages, plus your own.
Weight and reps, reps only, held time, distance and time, and cardio time exercises.
Workouts with supersets, circuits and work and rest intervals, planned on days of the week.
Live workout screen with last-time values, warm-up and to-failure sets, rest timer and stopwatch.
Records for weight, estimated one-rep max, volume, reps, time, distance and pace, with a notice when one is broken.
Charts per exercise, weekly totals, an activity calendar, sets per muscle group and streaks.
Weights and distances in pounds and miles or kilograms and kilometres according to the region.
Desktop window and public web page using the same Apps Hub profile.
Optional Health integration for workout minutes, calories and body data.
App API for reading workouts, logging sessions and managing exercises and workouts.

integrations.name: Health
integrations.summary: Optionally sends the minutes and estimated calories of finished workouts to Health, reads the profile's weight, height, age and sex, and shows activity that other apps sent to Health. Each profile chooses which links to enable.
integrations.requires: Health 1.4.0 or newer installed and its App API enabled in Apps Hub → Settings → App APIs. The App API is off by default.

integrations.name: Any app
integrations.summary: Lets other apps search exercises, read workouts, sessions, records and statistics, log finished workouts and manage the calling profile's own exercises and workouts.
integrations.requires: Fitness' App API enabled in Apps Hub → Settings → App APIs. The App API is off by default.

integrations.name: mvmAI
integrations.summary: The optional AI help asks mvmAI to build workouts from the exercises in Fitness and to review your progress. Suggested workouts are shown for review and nothing is saved until you confirm. It is generated by AI from the data you entered and is not medical advice.
integrations.requires: Fitness Premium build, the owner's AI help switch, mvmAI installed and its App API enabled in Apps Hub → Settings → App APIs. The App API is off by default.
